sentences.text: Lotosaurus was a heavily built quadruped measuring between 1.5 and 2.5 meters in length. It was a herbivore that used its toothless, beaked jaws to shear off leaves.
The animal possessed a sail on its back, giving it an appearance similar to Permian pelycosaurs like Dimetrodon, though the sail was not as high.
At least 38 individuals of Lotosaurus died in a single location, representing various ages.
Researchers suggest Lotosaurus may have died from thirst or sickness during the dry season while gathered around a watering hole.

The genus Lotosaurus was named by Fa-kui Zhang in 1975, with Lotosaurus adentus as the type species. The holotype of Lotosaurus is the well-preserved, articulated skeleton IVPP V 4881 (or possibly V 4880).
Modern cladistic analyses by Sterling J. Nesbitt in 2011 classified Lotosaurus as a member of the group Poposauroidea.
Lotosaurus fossils have been found in Hunan Province in central China. Evidence suggests Lotosaurus lived in a subtropical environment with distinct wet and dry seasons.
A 2019 study determined the maximum depositional age of the Lotosaurus fossils to be 238.0 ± 1.4 million years ago during the Ladinian stage.

It is debated whether Lotosaurus was endemic to the South China Craton or immigrated from the North China Craton, with immigration currently considered more likely due to the presence of relatives elsewhere.
